clue.text: Advanced one pound to get food

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it, so advanced means lent
the Roman numeral for one is I
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone borrowed a quid to buy a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advanced' looks like progress but is money handed over as a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentil is an edible pulse, a staple ingredient of soups and dals.

clue.text: Strongly objects to house charges around the Home Counties

indicators.note: around tells us the charges are wrapped about the counties, one piece enclosing the other

parts.note: rents are what tenants are charged for a house
SE, the south-east of England, is where the Home Counties lie around London

explanation.surface: A tenant grumbles about rent bills in the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in the south-east (SE) of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter indignation at it, taking strong objection.

clue.text: A demonstrative Chinese dynasty made by men of straw?

parts.note: that is a demonstrative pronoun or adjective, like this, these and those
the Ching (Qing) was the last imperial dynasty of China

explanation.surface: A pointing word and a Chinese dynasty somehow produced by scarecrows.
explanation.walkthrough: Ching is the older spelling of Qing. 'Men of straw' are usually weaklings or scarecrows; here they are roofers who work in straw.
explanation.definitionFit: Roofs covered in straw or reed are laid by craftsmen working the straw, hence the question mark.

clue.text: It is suggestive of Christian immorality

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks dates of the Christian era
vice is wickedness or immoral conduct

explanation.surface: Something hints at un-Christian sinfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (anno Domini, 'in the year of the Lord') stands for Christian by convention, from the Christian calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel puts forward suggestions, so it is something suggestive of a course of action.

clue.text: Awkward bosses completely dominate one's thoughts

indicators.note: awkward suggests something clumsy and out of order, so these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Difficult managers fill an employee's mind all day long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' rearranges BOSSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To preoccupy someone's mind continually and intrusively is the meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Unruly pets rove and go too far

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of the words that follow are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Badly behaved animals wander off and stray beyond their bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' rearranges PETS and ROVE together.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed a limit, literally stepping beyond a line, is to go too far.

clue.text: Drug checked by the traffic police

definitions.meaning: the rate a motorist travels at, monitored by radar

explanation.surface: A narcotic is being inspected by officers on the roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for amphetamine, and the rate of travel that traffic officers monitor with radar.

clue.text: The sort of heel which makes toes tilt

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters of the words named are formed into something new by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A very high heel forces the wearer's toes to tip forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges TOES and TILT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a tall, thin heel on a woman's shoe, named after the slim dagger.

clue.text: Colour of an iris gives protection against the sun

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the hue of the eye's coloured ring
a visor worn over the eyes to keep out glare

explanation.surface: An eye's colour somehow shields it from sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Split, it is the hue of the eye; whole, it is a visor worn to keep glare off the eyes.

clue.text: The first book is on hereditary factors

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so this piece follows the next

parts.note: genes are the units of heredity

explanation.surface: Scripture's opening volume turns out to be about genetics.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the hereditary factors come first and 'is' is tacked on behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening book of the Bible, telling of the creation, carries this name.

clue.text: Stealing an article by Foot

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Plagiarism of a piece written by a man named Foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital F on 'Foot' tempts one to think of a writer or politician; it is only the unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is the act of stealing, taking property without consent.

clue.text: Fast way to enter a convention uninvited when…

definitions.meaning: a strict regime of little food, a quick route to weight loss
to gatecrash an assembly, a diet being a formal conference

explanation.surface: A quick method of getting into a conference you weren't invited to.
explanation.walkthrough: A diet is also a formal assembly (the Diet of Worms), and to crash is to gatecrash. The ellipsis runs on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe short-term eating regime is a quick route to slimming; read literally, gatecrashing an assembly.

clue.text: Wry utterance from a gentleman of the road

indicators.note: an utterance is something spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the clue word

parts.note: wry means dryly mocking; said aloud it gives the entry

explanation.surface: A tramp makes a sardonic remark.
explanation.walkthrough: In Romany a rye is a gentleman, as in George Borrow's book The Romany Rye; the travelling life makes him one 'of the road'.
explanation.definitionFit: Romany usage gives the word for a gentleman, so a Romany gentleman on the road.

clue.text: … they lack established means ofentry

parts.note: continuing the previous clue: gatecrashers have no proper door key of their own, the usual way into a house

explanation.surface: Gatecrashers have no proper way to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 11 across: crashers lack the key that lets residents in.
explanation.definitionFit: A small key that opens a front door's spring lock is the regular way of getting in.

clue.text: Land used for a housing development

definitions.meaning: a large area of property in the country
a planned group of houses built together

explanation.surface: Ground set aside for building new homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A landed property, and a council or housing development of many homes.

clue.text: Shut your eyes to monkey business!

definitions.text: Shut your eyes to monkey business!

parts.words: Shut your eyes to monkey business!
parts.note: the three wise monkeys cover eyes, ears and mouth; the one with eyes covered gives this motto

explanation.surface: An order to ignore mischief going on around you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkey business' means mischief, but here it is the literal business of the three wise monkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: The motto of the wise monkey covering its eyes advises ignoring wrongdoing.

clue.text: Triangle needs reconstructing

indicators.note: the clue word needs changing, so its letters must be put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A geometric figure must be rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' says Triangle must be changed: rearrange its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Changing or modifying something is a form of rebuilding it.

clue.text: Cop proposes return of prohibition

indicators.note: return means the word is turned back, read from right to left

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: A police officer suggests reintroducing prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cop' looks like a noun, a police officer; it is the verb, to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop is slang for to catch or seize, as is to nab.

clue.text: Sets data out in the manner prescribed

indicators.note: out implies the letters are set out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lays out figures according to the regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SETS and DATA.
explanation.definitionFit: Done exactly according to what was laid down, following the instructions given.

clue.text: Take off a games lesson

parts.note: PE, physical education, is the school games lesson

explanation.surface: Removing clothes for a sports class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like undressing; it means mimic. PE is physical education, a school gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate or mimic someone, copying their manner, is to take them off.

clue.text: Throws wild parties

definitions.meaning: riotous sessions of revelry, or brief affairs

explanation.surface: Someone hosts riotous gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means hurls, and the plural noun means bouts of wild indulgence.

clue.text: He is elevated by the Queen

definitions.text: He is elevated by the Queen

parts.words: He is elevated by the Queen
parts.note: a man knighted by the monarch gains this title of address

explanation.surface: A man raised up by Her Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: To be knighted is to be elevated; a knight is addressed by this title before his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The title given to a knight, conferred by the sovereign.

clue.text: Classifies according to types

parts.note: as can mean according to, as in 'as directed'
sorts are kinds or types

explanation.surface: Someone groups items by their categories.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one plain definition, but 'according to' is a separate piece, as in 'as agreed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things into groups by kind is to classify them.

clue.text: One sister and one child working harmoniously

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a nun is a religious sister
a second I, the Roman numeral for one
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A nun and a boy co-operating nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'One' and 'one' give I.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together in agreement is the sense, from voices singing the same note.

clue.text: The guillotine for one of Louis XVI's ministers?

definitions.text: The guillotine for one of Louis XVI's ministers?

parts.words: The guillotine for one of Louis XVI's ministers?
parts.note: the blade dealt with heads by the neck

explanation.surface: The fate of a French royal minister during the Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Necker was finance minister to Louis XVI; humorously, a guillotine is something that goes for the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genevan banker who ran France's finances for Louis XVI bore this surname, which also suggests a neck-cutter.

clue.text: They are related in a presentation of scene!

indicators.note: a presentation of the word arranges its letters into a new display

parts.note: the setter's fodder: the letters of scene, which need an extra I to make six

explanation.surface: Relatives appear in a theatrical scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a presentation of' rearranges the fodder, but SCENE gives only five letters: the setter's fodder lacks the I needed for the six-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Daughters of one's brother or sister are relatives.

clue.text: Deviation put reader in a tizzy

indicators.note: in a tizzy means flustered and confused, so the letters are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A reader is flustered by a change of plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a tizzy' rearranges PUT and READER.
explanation.definitionFit: A departure from the norm is a deviation from it.

clue.text: Fit to go about a mile-at an easy pace?

indicators.note: about tells us one piece goes around the other

parts.note: able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: Someone fit enough strolls around a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ABLE around M.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk at a leisurely pace is to stroll in a relaxed manner.

clue.text: 'e'as to take steps to marry in a hurry

parts.note: the dropped h of Cockney speech: 'e for he
to lope is to run with long, easy strides

explanation.surface: A Cockney says he must take action to get married quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney 'e 'as to is 'he has to'; the dropped H leaves E.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off secretly to marry, often in haste.

clue.text: Tasty snippets of gossip

parts.note: small morsels of food and juicy fragments of news, both described in one phrase

explanation.surface: Juicy bits of news.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dainty morsels and choice pieces of scandal.

clue.text: Make light of injunction to eschew greatness

definitions.meaning: an order to stay small, split into two words

explanation.surface: Downplay an order to avoid grandeur.
explanation.definitionFit: Means to disparage; split in two it is a command to stay small.

clue.text: Consented to make a silver pipe

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a reed is a simple pipe or the vibrating part of one

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to fashion a silver flute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent is to assent, saying yes to a proposal.
